system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**, described as final. | **25% / AUD 6m** cap. The 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost; none is given. | **Reject 20%; seek 25% / AUD 6m.** The fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Replace both thresholds with the playbook figures and tipping recovery.** The seller’s thresholds materially narrow recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; seller proposes limits apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | General claims period of **24 months** after Completion; preserve distinct regimes for other claims. | **Reject 18 months and the blanket extension of limits to all claims.** The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate fundamental/title regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Require the separate regime.** Applying general limits would leave core ownership and authority risks inadequately protected. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims, with no stated fraud carve-out. | Carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Add the full carve-out; do not waive it.** The draft purports to restrict recovery even for deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Delete blanket general disclosure and require specific fair disclosure.** The current wording risks treating undisclosed detail as disclosed. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known or discoverable by the Buyer or its advisers, including from the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusion. Any qualifier must identify seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry; never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Reject the broad exclusion and replace only with a tightly limited seller-knowledge qualifier if needed.** Buyer diligence or discoverability should not broadly extinguish warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence conditions are currently included. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Make both consent and condition satisfaction evidenced pre-Completion conditions.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and delivery alone does not establish conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms no repayment or final discharge is included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payout, direct repayment and effective releases at Completion.** A later release leaves the Buyer exposed to continuing debt/security risk. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are left to the Seller and are not itemised in funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded; no silent exclusion. | **Require explicit treatment and funding of bonuses and applicable on-costs.** Otherwise the completion mechanics may leave the Buyer or Company bearing an unprovided liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 open, with no independent verification of non-payment or confirmatory assignment. | Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Broaden the indemnity and retain a workable cure for cleared payment and transfer.** The current scope may not protect against the full IP/assignment exposure, and the amount is unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure does not establish access, scope or notification duty and states no loss amount. | Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without asserting an unproven breach or loss.** The facts remain unresolved and should not be overstated or dismissed. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the three related renewals using DD-008 and DD-011 together; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate timing, scope, termination and accrual, but do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosure does not establish they are unavoidable or outside the ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override. Tax/IP terms remain open, with no assumed unlimited liability or resolution. | **Reject the blanket override and negotiate each category expressly.** General limitations must not silently collapse distinct protections or imply unresolved terms are agreed. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register as evidence Harbourglass holds 100%; no independent verification identified. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is only a supplied internal source. | **Require independent title and authority evidence.** The register alone is not independent proof of the relevant matters. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms **open**; assume neither unlimited liability nor a resolution. | **Do not accept the seller’s asserted settlement; negotiate and document Tax/IP terms separately.** The playbook records these terms as open, not agreed. |
=== END ADVICE ===
